acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC19: Dialogue buttons render with aria-expanded="false" by default
AC20: Clicking a dialogue button toggles aria-expanded to "true"
AC21: Clicking the button again (or clicking another button) resets aria-expanded to "false"
AC22: A test in dialogue-qa.test.ts verifies the aria-expanded attribute behaviour

All 336 GUI tests pass.

summary: Code review passed. The aria-expanded implementation in mcp-server/gui/public/views/work-package.js is correct across all three code paths: initial render (attribute set in HTML template at line 194), expand (setAttribute 'true' at line 246), same-button collapse (setAttribute 'false' at line 239), and different-button collapse (setAttribute 'false' at line 228). Logic is clear and symmetric. Four tests in dialogue-qa.test.ts (AC19–AC21) exercise each transition path with realistic DOM setup. All 26 dialogue-qa tests pass. No issues found.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and idiomatic vanilla JS. All three aria-expanded state transitions mirror the existing classList toggling pattern already present in the handler, making the change minimal and low-risk.

aria-expanded is set as a literal string attribute ('true'/'false') via setAttribute, which is the correct approach for ARIA boolean attributes in HTML — using a JS boolean would produce 'true' anyway but setAttribute makes the intent explicit.

The AC21 test for 'clicking a different button' correctly checks the intermediate state after btn1 click and the final state after btn2 click — this four-assertion sequence is exactly the right level of detail for a state-machine test.
